input.quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
input.rationale: No most-favoured-nation obligation is imposed on us anywhere in the agreement. The Charges provision (§ 4.1) simply provides that charges are set in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms, with no requirement that we extend IBM terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or match third-party offers; searches for MFN-style language ("most favoured/favored", "no less favorable", "best price/terms", "discount", "exclusive") returned no customer-side pricing or terms-parity obligation. Section 14.16 (Freedom of Action) confirms each party may contract freely with others. This meets the preferred position (no MFN burden on Customer), so no redline is proposed; the absence of a vendor-granted MFN in our favour is a commercial upside item to raise in negotiation rather than a playbook deviation.
